result.question:
I'm worried that urgent work on Transformer 1 at site MAIN is stuck behind an overloaded technician. Give me the MAIN site's work order KPIs for the last 6 months, including backlog, overdue count and average completion time. Then list every open work order on Transformer 1 with its number, description, priority, scheduled date and assigned technician, and flag which ones are overdue.

For each technician assigned to those work orders, count how many open work orders they currently hold at MAIN. Anyone holding more than 5 counts as overloaded.

Next, work out TDCG from the latest oil sample using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co only. Use these limits: Condition 1 up to 720 ppm, Condition 2 from 721 to 1920, Condition 3 from 1921 to 4630, and Condition 4 above 4630.

If Transformer 1 is at Condition 2 or higher, do the following for any overdue work order on it that sits with an overloaded technician. Reassign it to the technician with the fewest open work orders at MAIN, choosing among those who have worked on Transformer 1 before and are not overloaded. Give it a start date within the next 7 days that avoids any day with 3 or more scheduled work orders at MAIN. If it is Condition 1, don't reassign anything. Just list the overdue items and recommend a catch-up order, ranked by priority and then by how late they are.

If every technician with Transformer 1 history is overloaded, don't reassign. Tell me who is least loaded and recommend bringing in outside help. If any of the six gases is null in the latest sample, use its most recent non-null value and flag it as carried forward.
result.answer:
No further lookups are needed — I have the KPIs, the full MAIN work-order population, the schedule calendar, and the oil sample. Here's the assessment.

## 1. MAIN site KPIs (last 6 months)
| KPI | Value |
|---|---|
| Total work orders | 1 |
| Completed | 0 |
| Backlog | 1 |
| Overdue | 0 |
| Avg completion time | 0 hrs (no completions in period) |
| Priority breakdown | P1: 1 |
| Top asset | Transformer 1 (1 WO) |

## 2. Open work orders on Transformer 1
| WO # | Description | Priority | Scheduled start | Assigned technician | Overdue? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | OLTC inspection – on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking) | 1 | **None** (schedstart/targstart null) | **Unassigned** (no wplabor line) | **No** – no scheduled/target date exists, so it can't be flagged overdue by the system. ⚠️ Note: the long description mentions "Target start 2024-01-19", but that field was never populated. |

Status: APPR, work type PdM, reported 2026-09-30.

## 3. Technician load at MAIN (open WOs)
No technician is assigned to any Transformer 1 work order. For context, the only technicians with open work at MAIN:
- **MECHTECH2** – 1 open (1000046, Pump 3) → not overloaded
- **HVACTECH1** – 1 open (1000045, Chiller 6) → not overloaded

Nobody at MAIN holds more than 5 open work orders. **Your worry about an overloaded technician isn't the bottleneck — the issue is that 1000051 has never been assigned or scheduled at all.**

## 4. TDCG from latest oil sample (2024-01-19)
| Gas | ppm |
|---|---|
| Hydrogen | 2,850 |
| Methane | 7,400 |
| Ethane | 5,470 |
| Ethylene | 16,650 |
| Acetylene | 7 |
| CO | 32 |
| **TDCG** | **32,409 ppm → Condition 4** (>4,630) |

All six gases were non-null in the latest sample — nothing carried forward. Caveat: this sample is ~2.7 years old (latest telemetry available), so a fresh DGA is strongly advised.

## 5. Reassignment decision
Transformer 1 is at Condition 4, so the reassignment rule is triggered — but there is **nothing eligible to reassign**:
- 1000051 is not overdue by system dates and is not held by any technician (let alone an overloaded one).
- No technician has any prior Transformer 1 history (1000051 is the only WO ever raised on this asset, and it's unassigned), so the candidate pool for reassignment is empty.

Per your rule, I made no changes. **Least-loaded technicians:** MECHTECH2 and HVACTECH1, tied at 1 open WO each — neither has transformer/OLTC experience (mechanical and HVAC crafts).

**Recommendation:** Given Condition 4 TDCG (ethylene-dominated, consistent with a high-temperature thermal fault) and a P1 work order that is unassigned and unscheduled, bring in outside transformer/OLTC specialist help and get 1000051 scheduled immediately. The next 7 days (2026-09-30 → 2026-10-07) have **zero** scheduled work orders at MAIN, so any day is clear — I'd suggest the earliest available, 2026-10-01. If you'd like, I can assign a labor code and set a start date on 1000051 now.
